correctness.rationale: In the unit-directed prey-to-consumer chain with existing basal-to-apex shortcut, the trophic levels are prey averages and the original squared incoherence is (n-2)²/(2n). Every admissible missing forward edge is either internal i->j with j<=n-2 and skip h>=1, or apex-targeting i->n-1. In the internal case, local prey-average shifts of -h/2 propagate to the penultimate node and -h/4 to the apex, giving q_int²=[h²+(k-h/2)²]/[2(n+1)], k=n-2. Completing square gives unique nearest integer h=floor((2k+2)/5); half-ties are arithmetically impossible. Apex additions have q_apex²=2(k²-ki+i²)/[3(n+1)]>=k²/[2(n+1)], strictly above the attainable internal optimum for k>=2. The h=1 option shows strict improvement; leading ratio tends to 4/5. Independent Fraction computations recomputed each admissible edge for n=4..11 and verified all argmin sets.

evidence: Earlier Resultary formula for one acyclic edge on a pure rooted tree gives squared cost (depth(v)-depth(u)-1)^2/(2n), but assumes zero-coherence base tree and cannot quantify a second apex averaging interaction.

The 2014 foundation gives trophic coherence/stability models; the 2017 article gives motif families and stochastic assembly, without an exact global optimum over all missing forward edges on these chains.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general rooted-tree result is not logically stronger on the initial apex-omnivorous graph. The claimed two-edge interaction and integer argmin survive source-model and quantitative comparison.

evidence: The older theorem starts with q0=0 and one target of indegree two. Here q0²=(n-2)²/(2n)>0 and the extra internal edge shifts the already doubly fed apex by -h/4, producing the distinct quadratic h²+(k-h/2)².
Optimization balances two different incoherence sources and rules out apex-directed additions via a separate lower bound.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the one-link rooted-tree formula nor generic trophic-coherence definitions determine this competing-deviation optimization by substitution; a new two-target perturbation and integer minimization is necessary.

evidence: Both old and new formulas use Johnson-type prey-average trophic levels and squared deviation of trophic distances.

The old result starts from a rooted tree with a single incoming edge per nonbasal node; the new baseline is a directed path plus basal-to-apex feeding edge, with two prey at the apex before optimization.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Same normalization and terminology do not make the graph families equivalent. The presence of a preexisting extra edge changes all apex response terms, so the second augmentation is not an instance of the rooted-tree one-augmentation theorem.

originality.rationale: A prior exact one-added-link trophic-incoherence theorem for rooted out-trees is a closely related stronger graph-family statement, but its baseline requires every nonbasal node to have exactly one prey and q0=0. The submitted graph ALREADY contains the basal-to-apex omnivory edge, so its apex has two incoming prey and nonzero q0 before the new link; the older theorem cannot be reapplied to this second-edge setting. Johnson et al. define the metric and model food-web stability; Klaise-Johnson examine random motif assembly and omnivory rather than the deterministic all-n two-omnivory optimum. No inspected source supplies the unique optimal skip h=floor((2n-2)/5) and 4/5 ratio in this precise graph/metric. Priority is best-of-knowledge only.
residual_risks: The family is deliberately narrow; the result does not extend to arbitrary directed acyclic food webs, weighted links or several simultaneous added links.
An unlocated ecological network design theorem or thesis might give the same edge-augmentation minimizer.
No dynamical stability or ecosystem-management benefit is established from decreasing q².

evidence: Original graph must be an arborescence and have q0=0; second link after preexisting apex shortcut falls outside premises.

value.rationale: The motivating structural question is whether one additional feeding link can restore coherence after an apex shortcut already disrupts the chain. For every size, the exact non-apex optimal skip spans roughly 2/5 of the chain, its placement is translation-independent within allowed internal positions, and it reduces squared incoherence by asymptotically 20%. This is a natural complete constrained network-optimization classification on the established prey-average q metric, not an unsupported inference of biological stability.

limitations: Unweighted forward-only acyclic one-edge addition, fixed basal/apex topology; structural q metric only.
The finite checks do not prove the all-n optimizer; direct two-case quadratic calculation does.
